legal_authority: National Trails System Act, 16 U.S.C. §§ 1241–1251; designation codified in 16 U.S.C. § 1244(a)
local_managing_agency: Varies by site and segment; not assigned trail-wide
co_managing_agencies: Federal, state, Tribal, local, nonprofit, and private owners/managers participate on their respective lands and sites
blm_role_summary: BLM has documented land-management responsibility for portions of the national trail, including four named California route segments. This is limited to BLM-administered lands and does not establish BLM responsibility for the entire BRIM feature.
management_evidence_title: California NHT NPS planning page and BLM California trail page
trail_status: A congressionally designated network of historic routes, traces, sites, and retracement opportunities; not a single continuous maintained footpath.
route_representation: The designation includes a network of named routes, branches, cutoffs, surviving traces, roads, auto-tour approximations, and interpreted sites. Applegate, Lassen, Nobles, and Yreka are routes or branches of this national trail, not separate national designations.
length_qualifier: Statutory approximate length; NPS visitor pages often say more than 5,000 miles and may approach 8,000 miles when all alternates and spurs are counted.
states_crossed: Missouri; Kansas; Nebraska; Colorado; Wyoming; Idaho; Utah; Nevada; Oregon; California
trail_summary_short: A broad network of nineteenth-century emigrant routes from the Missouri River toward California and Oregon.
historic_or_scenic_significance: Nationally significant for the overland migration that reshaped settlement, transportation, economies, and landscapes in the nineteenth-century American West.
indigenous_context: The route network crosses the homelands of many Indigenous nations. Interpretation should address Indigenous persistence as well as displacement, violence, disease, resource loss, and other lasting effects of mass westward migration.
management_plan_title: California and Pony Express National Historic Trails Comprehensive Management and Use Plan / Final Environmental Impact Statement
source_notes: Length language varies by source because the designation contains numerous routes, branches, cutoffs, and spurs. GlobalID was not materialized in this research environment and remains a geometry/audit field, not the semantic join key.

legal_authority: National Trails System Act, 16 U.S.C. §§ 1241–1251; designation codified in 16 U.S.C. § 1244(a)
local_managing_agency: Varies by site and segment; not assigned trail-wide
co_managing_agencies: Federal, state, Tribal, local, nonprofit, and private owners/managers participate on their respective lands and sites
blm_role_summary: BLM identifies portions of the Pony Express National Historic Trail on BLM-managed lands in California, Colorado, Nevada, Utah, and Wyoming. This role is limited to those lands and does not make BLM the trail-wide administrator.
management_evidence_title: Pony Express NHT NPS planning page and BLM trail page
trail_status: A congressionally designated historic route and network of sites, traces, roads, and retracement opportunities; not a continuous clearly marked footpath.
route_representation: Original and adjusted mail routes, surviving traces and stations, interpreted sites, public trail segments, and auto-tour roads that may only approximate the historic route.
length_qualifier: Statutory approximate length; current NPS visitor materials variously describe the route as more than 1,800, nearly 1,900, or about 2,000 miles.
states_crossed: Missouri; Kansas; Nebraska; Colorado; Wyoming; Utah; Nevada; California
trail_summary_short: The 1860–1861 horseback mail route between St. Joseph, Missouri, and Sacramento, California.
historic_or_scenic_significance: Nationally significant for communications, transportation, commerce, and the enduring cultural memory of rapid horseback mail across the West.
indigenous_context: The route and its stations crossed Indigenous homelands and often relied on scarce water and travel corridors. NPS interpretation documents settler and mining encroachment, conflict, and resource pressures affecting Native communities, including events associated with the Pyramid Lake War.
management_plan_title: California and Pony Express National Historic Trails Comprehensive Management and Use Plan / Final Environmental Impact Statement
source_notes: Length differs among official summaries; the statutory approximate length is retained with the range explained. GlobalID remains blank because no live geometry snapshot was materialized.

legal_authority: National Trails System Act, 16 U.S.C. §§ 1241–1251; Old Spanish Trail Recognition Act of 2002
administering_agency: National Park Service and Bureau of Land Management (joint trail-wide administration)
local_managing_agency: Varies by land ownership and segment; not assigned trail-wide
co_managing_agencies: NPS and BLM jointly administer the national trail program; federal, state, Tribal, local, and private land managers retain responsibility for their respective lands and sites
blm_role_summary: BLM is a joint trail-wide administering agency with NPS. Joint administration does not imply that every mapped segment is jointly managed; local land management still follows jurisdiction and ownership.
management_evidence_title: Old Spanish National Historic Trail Comprehensive Administrative Strategy
trail_status: A multi-route historic-trail system with refined and approximate alignments, high-potential sites and segments, roads, and limited retracement opportunities; not a continuous recreational footpath.
route_representation: Armijo Route, Northern Route, North Branch, Mojave Road and related route refinements, high-potential segments and sites, auto-tour roads, and interpretive locations. Alignment refinement and digitization remain ongoing.
length_qualifier: Statutory approximate trail-system length; official pages commonly describe more than 2,700 miles.
states_crossed: New Mexico; Colorado; Arizona; Utah; Nevada; California
trail_summary_short: A network of pack-trade routes linking New Mexico and Southern California, especially during 1829–1848.
historic_or_scenic_significance: Nationally significant for transregional trade, travel, exploration, cultural exchange, and the movement of goods and people between New Mexico and California.
indigenous_context: The trail system crosses the homelands of many Tribal nations and drew upon Indigenous travel knowledge, labor, exchange networks, and landscapes. Interpretation should also address coercion, captivity and slave trading, violence, and the consequences of colonial expansion.
management_plan_title: Old Spanish National Historic Trail Comprehensive Administrative Strategy
source_notes: Joint administration is trail-wide program administration, not automatic joint local management of every segment. The 2017 alignment is authoritative for that planning product but remains subject to refinement.

official_name: Juan Bautista de Anza National Historic Trail
legal_authority: National Trails System Act, 16 U.S.C. §§ 1241–1251; Juan Bautista de Anza National Historic Trail Act
local_managing_agency: Varies by site and segment; not assigned trail-wide
co_managing_agencies: NPS administers through partnerships with Tribal governments, federal, state and local agencies, nonprofit organizations, private landowners, and Mexican institutions
blm_role_summary: BLM documents trail portions on BLM-managed lands in Arizona and California. BLM's role is limited to those lands and is not trail-wide administration.
management_evidence_title: 2023 Anza Foundation Document and BLM Anza trail page
trail_status: A historic corridor with a marked auto route, interpreted sites, and developed or certified recreational retracement segments; a continuous recreation trail remains an aspiration rather than a universal present condition.
route_representation: Historic expedition corridor, modern auto route that approximates the expedition, independently managed sites, and walking, bicycling, and equestrian retracement segments that may not occupy the exact historic trace.
length_qualifier: Current NPS description is approximately 1,200 miles in the United States; the Foundation Document describes an aspiration for a contiguous recreation route of more than 1,210 miles.
trail_summary_short: Commemorates the complex histories and landscapes of the 1775–1776 Spanish colonizing expedition to San Francisco Bay.
historic_or_scenic_significance: Nationally significant for Spanish imperial expansion, migration, settlement, military logistics, the founding of communities in Alta California, and the complex multicultural identities of expedition members and affected communities.
indigenous_context: The corridor crosses the homelands of more than 70 Tribal communities and follows paths used by Indigenous peoples for millennia. The 2023 Foundation Document states that Spanish colonization profoundly harmed Tribal worlds while emphasizing the persistence and continuing traditions of those communities.
management_plan_title: Juan Bautista de Anza National Historic Trail Comprehensive Management and Use Plan
source_notes: Use the 2023 Foundation Document for current purpose, significance, partnership, and interpretive framing; retain the 1996 comprehensive plan as the formal trail-wide management plan.

local_managing_agency: Varies by land-management unit and ownership along the trail
co_managing_agencies: U.S. Forest Service, National Park Service, Bureau of Land Management, Tribal, state, local, and private land managers on their respective portions
blm_role_summary: BLM manages portions of the PCT where it crosses BLM-administered lands; current Forest Service materials identify seven BLM field offices along the trail. BLM is not the trail-wide administering agency.
management_evidence_title: Pacific Crest NST Forest Service land-and-resources page
trail_status: A substantially continuous long-distance scenic trail, subject to official relocations, temporary closures, fire and storm damage, snow, permits, and land-manager-specific restrictions.
route_representation: Maintained long-distance trail centerline and official relocations. Even here, the GIS line is a reference representation rather than a survey, legal boundary, or guarantee of current passability.
length_qualifier: Current operational length used by the Forest Service; the 1968 statutory description estimated approximately 2,350 miles.
trail_summary_short: A long-distance scenic trail following the mountain ranges of California, Oregon, and Washington from Mexico to Canada.
historic_or_scenic_significance: One of the two original National Scenic Trails, protected for outstanding scenic and recreational values across the Pacific mountain ranges.
indigenous_context: The trail crosses the homelands and living cultural landscapes of many Tribal nations and includes Tribal lands and culturally significant places. Visitor language should emphasize respect for Tribal jurisdiction, cultural resources, and applicable restrictions.
management_plan_title: Pacific Crest National Scenic Trail Comprehensive Plan
source_notes: The 1982 comprehensive plan remains operative trail-wide guidance and is supplemented by the current Foundation Document. Conditions and permit links are partner-operated in formal agency coordination; local manager rules still control.

legal_authority: National Trails System Act, 16 U.S.C. §§ 1241–1251; Butterfield Overland National Historic Trail Designation Act
local_managing_agency: Varies by site and segment; not assigned trail-wide
co_managing_agencies: NPS administers through consultation and partnerships; federal, state, Tribal, local, and private land managers retain responsibility for resources under their jurisdiction
blm_role_summary: The BLM California feature service establishes data stewardship and source context, not a segment-specific management assignment. A trail-specific BLM land-management role for the BRIM Butterfield feature was not verified and is intentionally left unknown pending direct segment evidence.
management_evidence_title: Butterfield NHT NPS management and comprehensive-plan pages; BLM CA GIS metadata
trail_status: A newly designated national historic trail represented by historic route corridors, surviving traces, structures, landmarks, roads, and interpreted sites; not a continuous traditional trail.
route_representation: Approximately 3,292 miles following the Ox-Bow Route as generally depicted on the 15 study maps incorporated by the designation law. The GIS and interactive map are reference representations and do not imply access or an exact surviving trace.
length_qualifier: Statutory approximate length following the study-route maps; current NPS visitor materials commonly say almost 3,300 miles.
states_crossed: Missouri; Tennessee; Arkansas; Oklahoma; Texas; New Mexico; Arizona; California
trail_summary_short: The 1858–1861 overland mail and passenger route from St. Louis and Memphis through the southern United States to San Francisco.
historic_or_scenic_significance: Nationally significant for communications, commerce, passenger travel, technological change, and the federal effort to connect eastern and western populations before the Civil War.
indigenous_context: The designated route overlays much older Indigenous travel corridors and homelands. The NPS special-resource study consulted 49 Tribes, and Tribal comments emphasized that the landscape's history extends far beyond the 1858–1861 mail operation and should not be reduced to a settler transportation narrative.
management_plan_title: Butterfield Overland National Historic Trail Comprehensive Plan (draft; not final)
source_notes: The designation law names eastern termini at St. Louis, Missouri, and Memphis, Tennessee, producing an eight-state statutory route; the current NPS web header lists seven states and omits Tennessee. This package follows the statute and records the discrepancy. The 2026 draft comprehensive plan public review closed July 3, 2026; NPS was reviewing comments on August 4, 2026. The completed 2018 Special Resource Study remains the closest final route-wide study until the comprehensive plan is finalized. No BLM office or local manager was inferred from GIS publication or overlap.
closest_final_study_title: 2018 Butterfield Overland Trail Special Resource Study (final)
hover_admin_summary: Admin: NPS · BLM role not verified
